result.summary: The image shows a wide urban street with sidewalks on both sides, including a very wide walkway on the right featuring a bike-share station. While pedestrian space is provided, the lack of marked crossings and the wide roadway width may encourage higher vehicle speeds in a mixed residential and institutional context.

hazards.name: Wide travel lanes
hazards.description: The wide, open roadway design may encourage vehicle speeds higher than appropriate for a residential and institutional area.

hazards.name: Lack of mid-block crossing
hazards.description: Pedestrians may need to cross this wide street to reach the bike share or the large building on the right, but no marked crossing is provided.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the roadway between the residential and institutional buildings

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Install a marked mid-block crosswalk with appropriate signage to provide a legal and visible crossing point.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Add curb extensions (bulb-outs) to reduce the crossing distance and slow turning traffic at the nearest intersection.

interventions.title: Protected Bike Lane
interventions.description: Convert the wide shoulder or excess roadway width into a protected bike lane to narrow the travel lanes and provide a buffer for pedestrians.

result.summary: The image shows a wide, well-maintained concrete sidewalk adjacent to a brick building with decorative leaf art and bike racks. While the pedestrian walkway is spacious and clear of obstructions, there is no physical buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway, and the building frontage is relatively inactive at eye level.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical separation or planting strip between the wide sidewalk and the active roadway, increasing the risk of vehicle-pedestrian conflict.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line separating the sidewalk from the asphalt.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Buffer/Planting Strip
interventions.description: Install a planting strip or furniture zone with trees or bollards to provide physical and psychological separation between pedestrians and moving traffic.

interventions.title: Street Lighting Improvements
interventions.description: Add pedestrian-scale street lighting poles to improve visibility and safety during nighttime hours, as only building-mounted lighting is currently visible.

result.summary: The environment features wide travel lanes and parallel parking that likely encourage higher vehicle speeds. While wide sidewalks are present, there is a notable lack of marked pedestrian crossings or traffic calming measures despite the presence of a school crossing sign.

hazards.name: Long crossing distance
hazards.description: The wide roadway requires pedestrians to cross multiple lanes and parking zones without a refuge island.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the center of the roadway

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: Despite a school crossing sign, there are no visible painted crosswalks to guide pedestrians or alert drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Near the school crossing sign on the right side of the road

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks to increase visibility of pedestrian crossing points, especially near the school zone.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at potential crossing points to shorten the crossing distance and improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Speed Humps
interventions.description: Implement vertical traffic calming to reduce vehicle speeds in this area which appears to be near a recreation center and school.

result.summary: The image shows a residential street with row houses where the pedestrian environment is compromised by a narrow sidewalk and a large tree obstructing the walkway. There is a significant gap in the sidewalk network where the residential frontage ends, and no formal crossing infrastructure is visible.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: A large mature tree trunk occupies almost the entire width of the paved sidewalk, forcing pedestrians into the roadway or onto private property.
hazards.location_in_image: Center-right, in front of the first row house

hazards.name: Sidewalk Discontinuity
hazards.description: The paved sidewalk terminates abruptly at the end of the residential block, leaving no safe path along the adjacent fenced lot.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles and the large tree trunk create significant blind spots for drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image along the curb

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening/Bulb-out
interventions.description: Expand the sidewalk into the parking lane around the tree to maintain a continuous, ADA-compliant clear walking path.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Extension
interventions.description: Complete the sidewalk network by paving the walkway along the fenced lot to ensure pedestrian continuity.

interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the end of the block to improve visibility and reduce the crossing distance for pedestrians.
